metadata.author: Gheorghe Burnei
metadata.subject: 1.1. Background Context: Over the last 50 years, the developments emerged in the diagnosis and treatment of supracondylar humerus fractures (SHF) have significantly reduced the number of severe complications while certain complications with dreadful evolution, such as elbow stiffness or Volkmann's syndrome, have completely vanished. During my residency, in 1982, on the suggestion of Prof. Pesamosca, I have performed a surgical intervention for a patient diagnosed with SHF. At that time, the PP with K -wires were placed in an inverted V. The most common complication was the loss of reduction and the consequences seen in many cases were cubitus varus, cubitus valgum, abchilosis or stiffness. The inverted V-fixation was taken from Prof. Vereanu. I asked his permission to cross K-wires and he agreed. It was the first X-fixation. I showed Prof. Vereanu the x-rays and we followed-up the patient together. We found an improvement in the patient's postoperative evolution.
